controls.label: Query matrix Q
controls.help: Changes the dot products in Scores S, which changes Weights A and Output O.

controls.label: Key matrix K
controls.help: Changes the dot products in Scores S, which changes Weights A and Output O.

controls.label: Value matrix V
controls.help: Does not change Scores S or Weights A; it changes the weighted average that forms Output O.

controls.label: Key dimension dk
controls.help: Sets the divisor sqrt(dk) applied to Scores S, which changes Weights A and Output O; it has no effect while scaling is off.

controls.label: Apply 1/sqrt(dk) scaling
controls.help: Turns the divisor on or off, changing Scores S, then Weights A and Output O.

explorations.title: All dot products equal
explorations.instruction: Predict: if every score in a row is the same number, what will the weights look like? Then apply the preset, which sets Q, K, V, dk and turns scaling off.
explorations.observe: Scores S show 1 in all four cells, Weights A show 0.5 in all four cells, Row sums R stay at 1 for both queries, and Output O has 0.5 in every cell.
explorations.why: Every weight is exp(s)/sum of exp(s) over the same s, so a row of identical scores gives identical weights, here exactly two halves; the output row then sits halfway between the two value rows.

explorations.title: One dominant dot product
explorations.instruction: Predict: how concentrated will the weights be when one score is 4 and the other is 0? Then apply the preset, which sets Q, K, V, dk and turns scaling off.
explorations.observe: Scores S show 4 and 0 in each row, Weights A show about 0.982 and 0.018, Row sums R stay at 1, and Output O keeps almost all of value row 1.
explorations.why: The softmax exponentiates the scores, and exp(4) is about 54.6 while exp(0) is 1, so the first key receives about 98 percent of the weight. Switching scaling on would divide both scores by sqrt(dk), shrinking the gap between them and pushing the weights back toward uniform.
